title: Session-Resilient Toolflow & SDK Ergonomics Proposal
summary: Framing a pragmatic PRD for session-resilient streaming + tool-calling that prioritizes SDK ergonomics. Introduces the idea of lightweight session checkpoints and delta-replay to make client-integrations tolerant of network loss, restarts, and mid-flight tool invocations while keeping server-side complexity bounded.
goals: 1) Define an incremental streaming contract that supports durable sessions and fast reconnection. 2) Specify a tool-call handshake that survives partial failures and enables deterministic replay on reconnect. 3) Recommend SDK surfaces (sync/async) that make resilience easy for integrators without exposing low-level plumbing. 4) Provide rollout milestones and safety gates for progressive adoption.
non_goals: 1) Replace existing full session persistence for Dedicated/Private—this is an incremental hosted-focused approach. 2) Provide a full language binding for every runtime—scope is API + JS/TS SDK patterns and a canonical reference client. 3) Solve end-to-end idempotency across client-side actions (we aim to provide built-in primitives, not business logic guarantees).
primary_user_flows:
- Mobile chat app: background/foreground reconnects, join-in-progress sessions, resume partial tool execution.
- Web editor: user triggers actions (e.g., code-run) while network flaky; wants deterministic result or graceful fallback.
- Server-side orchestrator: multiple agents call hosted-api and need reproducible outcomes after an autoscaler restart.
api_contract_sketch:
High level: sessions are short-lived objects with stable ids and monotonic checkpoints.

Endpoints (sketch):
POST /v1/sessions -> { session_id, ephemeral_key, created_at }
POST /v1/sessions/{id}/append-stream -> chunked streaming body or websocket frames, optional checkpoint header X-Checkpoint: <seq>
GET /v1/sessions/{id}/events?from_checkpoint=<n> -> stream of events since checkpoint n (supports replay)
POST /v1/sessions/{id}/tool-call -> { call_id, tool, input, idempotency_token } -> returns immediate ack + later result event via events stream
PATCH /v1/sessions/{id}/checkpoint -> { checkpoint_seq, kv_hash } -> used by clients to mark durable progress

Notes: session keys TTL is short; clients reauthenticate to create new ephemeral keys if needed.
streaming_semantics:
- Checkpoints are small numeric sequence numbers; events include checkpoint metadata.
- Server guarantees at-least-once delivery of events for a checkpoint range; clients must be prepared for duplicates.
- Reconnect flow: client asks for events from last local checkpoint; server streams missing events and provides new stream.
- Prefix caching: server may fast-path events that are continuations of a known prefix (optimizes hot sessions).
- Batching: clients can supply a soft-latency budget header to let the runtime batch small messages for cost savings; default is low-latency mode.
tool_call_protocol:
- Two-phase tool calls: CALL (ack) then RESULT (event).
- CALL includes an idempotency_token and a lightweight deterministic 'spec' used to detect semantic idempotency on replay.
- Tool execution can be long-running; RESULT is delivered as an event with status {ok|error|cancelled|partial}.
- Partial results: tool runtimes can emit intermediate events tagged with partial=true and an interim checkpoint.
- Cancellation: client may POST /cancel with call_id; server best-effort cancels. Clients should treat cancellation as informational, not guaranteed.
sdk_surface_guidelines:
- Primary primitives: Session.create(), Session.appendStream(frame), Session.on('event', cb), Session.checkpoint(), Session.callTool(spec, opts).
- Ergonomics: SDKs should surface a small 'reconnect policy' config (backoff, max-retries, resume vs restart) and expose an easy .resumeFrom(checkpoint) helper.
- Streaming abstraction: provide both async iterator and event-emitter styles; prefer async iterator for simple linear consumers.
- Tool-call helpers: callTool returns a 'handle' with .on('result'), .cancel(), and a promise for finalResult. The handle transparently performs idempotency on reconnects using stored tokens.
- Resource limits: SDK should enforce local buffer caps and expose hooks for when the client is behind (onBackpressure).
- Diagnostics: expose dbg().captureTrace() that emits a compact fidelity ladder snapshot (last N checkpoints, outstanding calls) to assist debugging without full logs.
rollout_milestones:
- M1 (Alpha): API prototypes + JS reference SDK; internal integrators only.
- M2 (Beta): Opt-in hosted endpoint; enable by tenant flag; add observability (per-session metrics).
- M3 (GA): Default session-resume behavior; SDKs 1.0; docs and migration guide; safety gate: <5% spurious duplicate tool runs in canary.
- M4: Add server-side opt-in for cross-region session fallback and session transfer (future).
open_questions:
- Duplication surface: how do we instrument and surface duplicate tool executions to customers without spamming alerts?
- Checkpoint frequency: what is the sweet spot default for mobile vs server workloads?
- Security: how do ephemeral session keys map to tenant-level audit logs without leaking ephemeral ids?
- Cost model: do we meter replayed events differently? If so, how to communicate to customers?
- Long-running tool calls: do we offer a separate 'durable tool' contract with stronger guarantees for Dedicated customers?
approvals: Product: Maya Patel (draft). Engineering review pending: Jonah Edwards, Aria Lopez. Security & Compliance consult queued (security@redwood).
notes_to_reviewers: This is intentionally pragmatic: keep server semantics weakly consistent (at-least-once) and push deterministic reconciliation to SDK + integrator. Focus review on: SDK ergonomics and the expected developer mental model for replay/duplicates. We should avoid adding heavyweight server-side transaction machinery in the initial rollout.
